exposure: hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HDP) with concurrent autoimmune comorbidities or manifestations
pregestational or early-gestation diagnosis of systemic autoimmune disease
de novo autoimmune manifestations first recognised in pregnancy
outcome: cardiac output and diastolic dysfunction markers
cohort: The study included 198 pregnant patients diagnosed with hypertensive disorders and either pre-existing autoimmune comorbidities or de novo autoimmune manifestations during pregnancy.
finding: The group with pre-existing autoimmune disease exhibited higher rates of severe preeclampsia, earlier gestational age at delivery, increased need for critical-care support, and greater fetal growth restriction and NICU admissions compared to those with de novo manifestations.
